MODULE 3: FULL OUTLINE

GAME TIME

Basketball School

I-ON-2 CONVERSION INTO 2-ON-1 BACK

12 MIN

BINDING YES NO

### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets (cut the court along rim line to create two playing spaces per basket)

### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per group

### DESCRIPTION

Players will be divided into groups of three. The offense and defense must stay in half of the full-court area, playing from sideline to rim line. Cones may be used to mark out the rim line. One player will start on the baseline with a ball facing half-court. One defender will guard the ball-handler from the baseline to the free-throw line, and another defender will play defense between the free-throw line and half-court line. The offensive player must attempt to dribble to the half-court line to score a 'touchdown' within 10 seconds, without losing possession of the ball. The defenders can only stay in their areas. If the offense scores a 'touchdown' or the defense forces a turnover (steal, out of bounds, time limit), it changes to a 2-on-1 at the same basket (with offense and the defense switching roles). Ensure only two groups play on one basket at a time.

### SCORING

The ball-handler will get 3 points for successfully completing a touchdown. In the 2-on-1, the offensive players will get 2 points for made baskets.

### KEY CONCEPTS

- Handling pressure
- Disruptive defense

### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- Defenders can only use one hand to defend.
- Remove the first defender's space limitations while keeping the second defender's limitations.
- Add another offensive player so that it is 2-on-2.
- Add in the 'rugby' load where offensive players can only pass laterally or backwards.

### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "Where is the space?"
- "What is the best shot to obtain within the 2-on-1?"

### STAFF ROLE

- Ensure players stay in their respective areas.
- Count down from 10 seconds.

Load for younger players

MODULE 3: FULL OUTLINE

GAME TIME

Basketball School

I-ON-I-I CREATE SEPARATION

16 MIN

BINDING YES NO

### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets (cut the court along rim line to create two playing spaces per basket)

### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per group

### DESCRIPTION

Players will work in groups of three. The offense and defense must stay in half of the full-court area, playing from sideline to rim line. Cones may be used to mark out the rim line. One player will start on offense, one on defense, and one as the 'facilitator.' The facilitator's job is to help the offense to score. The offensive player can pass to them and receive the ball back, as well as use the facilitator to screen for them. The offense has three dribbles on every catch to score. The facilitator can move around freely, and the offensive player should start in different locations. Ensure only two groups play on one basket at a time.

### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- The defender must play defense with one hand behind their back
- Players receive a bonus point for scoring inside the charge circle
- Players have no dribbles

### STAFF ROLE

- Ensure only two groups play on one basket at a time.
- Help the facilitator be proactive in creating an advantage for the offensive player.

### SCORING

Offensive players will get 2 points or 3 points for made baskets.

### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "How could you help your teammate to score?"
- "Defensively, how could you disrupt your opponent to make it more challenging?"

### KEY CONCEPTS

- Facilitator exploring ways to create advantages
- Disruptive defense
- Creative finishing

MODULE 3: FULL OUTLINE

GAME TIME

Basketball School

3-ON-3 SCRAMBLE

10 MIN

BINDING YES NO

### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per group

### DESCRIPTION

Three offensive players will start in different spacings outside the 3PT line and three defenders will begin anywhere inside the paint. The defense will start with the ball and pass to any offensive player. From here, a live 3-on-3 begins. The defense must scramble and attempt to recover back to neutral to cancel the advantage. Games will last until a basket is made or there is a defensive stop (defensive rebound or forced turnover). Repeat for three repetitions before the offense and defense switch roles.

### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- Remove one defender and play 3-on-2 if too difficult for the offense.
- A coach throws the pass in instead of the defense, making the scramble more unpredictable. This means the defense must communicate to confirm who is covering the ball as they closeout.
- Offense plays from a different spacing each time.
- The offense must dribble/sprint to the half-court line while the defense must touch the sideline in order to transition in between repetitions.

### SCORING

Offensive players will get 2 points or 3 points for made baskets.

### STAFF ROLE

- Make sure the defense starts inside the paint.
- Remind defenders to call 'ball' on closeouts.
- Help with the dynamic start load to transition between repetitions.

### KEY CONCEPTS

- Scrambling and locating match-ups
- Defense recovering back to neutral

### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "How can we closeout to prevent a wide open shot?"
- "How can the offense keep their advantage?"
